extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Plato; students of political philosophy and classical literature
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting the design principles and legislative prescriptions Socrates outlines for the guardian class and the ideal city (Book V of Plato's Republic), including education, breeding, family arrangements, and laws intended to secure unity and virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians' education: music and gymnastic
rubrics_metrics.description: The education which was assigned to the men was music and gymnastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women must be taught music and gymnastic and also the art of war, which they must practise like the men; education must be the same where duties are the same. Examples: women exercising in the palaestra, wearing armour, riding horseback—initial ridicule expected but justified by reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of duties for women and men (where appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: If women are to have the same duties as men, they must have the same nurture and education; the same pursuits which make a man a guardian will make a woman a guardian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences of physical strength acknowledged (lighter labours to women), but selection and assignment of civic roles depend on nature/gifts rather than sex per se. Anti-pattern: assuming sex alone dictates civic function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by nature and capacity, not by sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Men and women alike possess the qualities which make a guardian; those women who have such qualities are to be selected as companions and colleagues of men who resemble them in capacity and character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is based on gifts (healing, music, gymnastic, military spirit, philosophy, etc.) and moral/psychological fitness. The argument requires distinguishing meaningful differences of nature (affecting pursuits) from irrelevant differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership of wives and children
rubrics_metrics.description: The wives of our guardians are to be common, and their children are to be common, and no parent is to know his own child, nor any child his parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a means to unity: removing private familial ties creates a single familial sentiment among guardians. The claim of utility is asserted first; possibility and implementation to be treated separately and defended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community living: common houses and common meals
rubrics_metrics.description: They must live in common houses and meet at common meals. None of them will have anything specially his or her own; they will be together, and will be brought up together, and will associate at gymnastic exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communal life reinforces unity and shared feeling; prevents private possessions/attachments that create discord. Implementation detail: shared domestic arrangements among guardian class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeding policy: unite the best with the best
rubrics_metrics.description: The best of either sex should be united with the best as often, and the inferior with the inferior, as seldom as possible; they should rear the offspring of the one sort of union, but not of the other, if the flock is to be maintained in first-rate condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: maintain and improve the guardian stock. Requires active management and secrecy; those not to be reared (inferior or deformed offspring) are to be disposed of in unknown ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lawful falsehoods (noble lie) as a ‘medicine’ for the State
rubrics_metrics.description: Our rulers will find a considerable dose of falsehood and deceit necessary for the good of their subjects: the use of all these things regarded as medicines might be of advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Falsehoods must be controlled (known only to rulers) to prevent rebellion; compared to medical regimen—acceptable when for the good of the city. Anti-pattern: making such falsehoods public, which would undermine the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled mating via public festivals and engineered lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint certain festivals at which we will bring together the brides and bridegrooms ... invent some ingenious kind of lots which the less worthy may draw on each occasion of our bringing them together, and then they will accuse their own ill-luck and not the rulers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism for directing unions while preserving appearance of chance. Brave and better youth may be granted greater facilities for intercourse; lots and ritual as social cover for directed breeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of offspring: custody and exposure of inferior or deformed children
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper officers ... will take the offspring of the good parents to the pen or fold, and there they will deposit them with certain nurses ... but the offspring of the inferior, or of the better when they chance to be deformed, will be put away in some mysterious, unknown place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers control which children are reared in the guardian fold to maintain quality. Secret disposal of unfit offspring is prescribed as a means of eugenic population control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional rearing: use of nurses and wet-nurses; mothers relieved
rubrics_metrics.description: They will provide for their nurture, and will bring the mothers to the fold when they are full of milk, taking the greatest possible care that no mother recognises her own child; other wet-nurses may be engaged if more are required ... the mothers will have no getting up at night or other trouble, but will hand over all this sort of thing to the nurses and attendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Child-rearing is institutionalized to prevent parental bonds and to free mothers from domestic burdens. Emphasizes organized nursery arrangements and rotation of caregivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime breeding ages defined
rubrics_metrics.description: A woman at twenty years of age may begin to bear children to the State, and continue to bear them until forty; a man may begin at five-and-twenty ... and continue to beget children until he be fifty-five.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strictly enforce age windows for sanctioned procreation; conceptions outside prescribed ages viewed as illegitimate and subject to penalties (the child conceived is treated as uncertified and unconsecrated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning and prohibitions concerning relations and incest
rubrics_metrics.description: A man may not marry his daughter or his daughter's daughter, or his mother or his mother's mother; and women ... are prohibited from marrying their sons or fathers, or son's son or father's father ... if the lot favours them, and they receive the sanction of the Pythian oracle, the law will allow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generational marriage prohibitions with narrow exceptions allowed by divinatory sanction (oracle). Also a system of naming births by hymeneal dates to mask actual parentage and to define sibling relations for marriage prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offspring dating and naming to conceal parentage
rubrics_metrics.description: Dating from the day of the hymeneal, the bridegroom ... will call all the male children who are born in the seventh and tenth month afterwards his sons, and the female children his daughters ... All who were begotten at the time when their fathers and mothers came together will be called their brothers and sisters, and these ... will be forbidden to inter-marry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A calendrical naming system hides biological parentage and enforces social sibling bonds that prevent incestuous marriages; used to operationalize the communal family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrimony sanctified to serve the common good
rubrics_metrics.description: Make matrimony sacred in the highest degree, and what is most beneficial will be deemed sacred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ritualizing marriage (hymeneals, sacrifices, hymns by poets) both conceals and legitimizes the rulers' management of breeding. Sanctity tied to social utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign lighter labours to women due to comparative weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: In the distribution of labours the lighter are to be assigned to the women, who are the weaker natures, but in other respects their duties are to be the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge physical differences while maintaining equality of civic functions; specifics of labor distribution follow from comparative strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must obey laws and embody their spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardians must themselves obey the laws, and they must also imitate the spirit of them in any details which are entrusted to their care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians must combine willingness to obey with the power to command. Moral example and internalization of law required; rulers must not merely rule but live by the laws they enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity through shared pleasures and pains as the chief aim
rubrics_metrics.description: There is unity where there is community of pleasures and pains—where all the citizens are glad or grieved on the same occasions of joy and sorrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legislator's chief aim is to minimize discord and maximize common feeling (reduce private 'mine'/'not mine'). Communal family, common meals and property, and shared rearing of children are justified as means to unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology must reflect practice: act like a family, not only name one
rubrics_metrics.description: Shall they be a family in name only; or shall they in all their actions be true to the name? ... the language of harmony and concord will be more often heard than in any other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social roles and terms (father, brother, etc.) should imply real duties, reverence and care; performative naming without behavior undermines the political aim of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify relevant differences of nature before assigning roles
rubrics_metrics.description: When we assigned different pursuits to different natures we never considered ... what was the meaning of sameness or difference of nature; differences should be only those which affected the pursuit in which the individual is engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid verbal disputation: only distinctions that affect capacity to perform a civic function should justify different assignments. Example anti-pattern: extending difference-of-nature to irrelevant features (bald vs hairy).
